Identity.History: The Seleucid Empire arose from the eastern territories of Alexander the Great’s conquests and was founded by Seleucus I Nicator in the late 4th century BC. At its height it stretched from Anatolia and Syria to Mesopotamia and Iran. Its rulers promoted Hellenistic cities, trade, and military settlement, but constant wars with rival kingdoms, local revolts, and Parthian expansion steadily reduced the empire until Rome absorbed its last Syrian territories.
